entries.rationale: This is a direct symbolic membership/subset check on a finite set, including nested set elements. It has no spatial, interval, region, case, or graph dependency, so a visual adds no decisive reasoning value.

The item tests whether membership is objectively determined for three verbal collections. The definition-of-a-set judgment is textual and categorical; no visual medium is needed to represent the decisive step.

A three-set Venn can organize the union/intersection of the divisor sets A6, A9, and A4, but every membership is finite and directly enumerable. The visual is a helpful organizational aid, not a required carrier of the reasoning.

The item is controlled by the interval A, the two infinite rays in B, open/closed endpoint behavior, A union B, and the exact A minus B interval. A number line is the faithful medium for the decisive boundary and interval relationships.

The answer follows directly from the finite-set cardinality formula: four elements give 2^4 subsets, and excluding the full set leaves 15 proper subsets. No region, interval, case, or graph representation is needed.
